function.mechanism: Inert metallic particles/leaf remain largely unreactive and provide reflective metallic appearance when applied as surface coating.

adi.basis: EFSA re-evaluation (2016) did not set a numerical ADI; opinion characterized gold as of minimal toxicological concern with low estimated exposure but acknowledged data uncertainty.

efsa.key_finding: Authorized in EU for limited decorative uses; no numerical ADI set; low exposure estimates and uncertainty due limited data.

adi.basis: JECFA entry states 'NO ADI ALLOCATED' (1977) with comment 'Very limited use. Not considered to present a hazard'; 2018 note says not re-evaluated and Codex provisions withdrawn at CCFA50.

concerns.summary: A 90-day mouse study with food-grade gold reported sex-dependent shifts in gut microbiota and local immune markers at human-relevant dose framing.
Oral rat nanoparticle study reported dose/size-related accumulation and renal histopathology at higher exposures, while many routine clinical markers remained unchanged.
Nanoparticle-focused reviews raise theoretical concern that nanoscale fractions may alter uptake and toxicity relative to bulk inert metal assumptions.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA (2016) and JECFA historical conclusions did not identify a clear hazard at reported uses and did not assign a restrictive numerical ADI.
US FDA permits gold as a color additive exempt from certification with specific use constraints under 21 CFR 73.129.

adi_exceedance.notes: No numeric ADI is established (EFSA non-numeric; JECFA no ADI allocated), so formal ADI exceedance cannot be computed; EFSA-reported exposure estimates were low but uncertain due sparse use data.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory approvals and low estimated exposure support low-to-limited concern, but unresolved nanoparticle characterization and recent animal evidence of microbiome/immune and organ-level effects prevent classifying E175 as risk_free or simply limited with high confidence.
key_factors: EFSA 2016 non-numeric ADI with low exposure estimates and acknowledged uncertainty
FDA approval as color additive exempt from certification with strict conditions in 21 CFR 73.129
JECFA historical 'NO ADI ALLOCATED' with 2018 note of no re-evaluation/Codex provision withdrawal
Recent animal data indicating biologic effects at oral exposure
